**1** **INTRODUCTION**
**Summary**
Financial statement fraud detection is a significant topic and a challenging task related
to countless applications such as financial sectors, insurance, government agencies,
law enforcement and so on. This article presents an unsupervised learning model to
identify the financial fraud statements using the hybrid convolutional neural network.
The fraud detection scheme can be performed using a few stages: data preprocessing,
sampling, feature extraction, feature selection, clustering, and classification methods.
The preprocessing and sampling processes are used to clean and recognize duplicate
data. Then, the proposed model analyzes both text features and financial variables
to provide the best classification of financial statement fraud. In this article, a new
~~fuzzy red deer’s algorithm is proposed for selecting the optimal feature set, which~~
can improve the classification accuracy of the fraud prediction model. Subsequently,
an adaptive density based clustering (ADBC) approach is introduced for labeling the
selected features through the clustering process. Finally, the fraud statements are
predicted by proposing a hybrid CNN-MRFO model wherein the hyperparameters of
the CNN model are optimized through the MRFO learning algorithm. The simulation
results prove the effectiveness of the proposed model in terms of accuracy (98.85%),
precision (98.62%) and F-measure (99.32%).

The major contributions of the proposed hybrid model are:
**•** To introduce a hybrid unsupervised learning model CNN-MRFO for the detection of financial statement fraud with improved accuracy and
minimum processing time.
**•** The presented hybrid model can effectively and quickly handle the huge amount of data with data mining based text feature extraction and
extraction of financial statements.

**2** **RELATED WORK**
Some of the works related to the detection of financial fraud statements are discussed as follows:
Chimonaki et al. [16] presented the detection of financial statement fraud by machine learning with computational intelligence (CI) techniques.
The authors collected the data sample of 2469 comments from 2002 to 2015 to recognize the falsified financial statements. Research gaps were
recognized by illustrating the association among CI-based detection algorithms and financial statement fraud. The classification of false statements
was detected using the wrapped based models. The accuracy achieved with KNN was (89.11%) and NB was (68.29%). The error rate was lower
(9.92%) when using the KNN classifier. The major drawbacks were overfitting and computationally expensive. Jan [17] established an effective fraud
detection in financial statements for the development of sustainable financial markets. The detection methodology was based on two stages. At
the initial stage, the significant variables were screened by a support vector machine (SVM) and artificial neural network (ANN). In the next phase,
four classes of decision trees, namely, quick unbiased efficient statistical tree (QUEST), C5.0, chi-square automatic interaction detector (CHAID),
and classification and regression tree (CART) were created for classification. Both nonfinancial and financial variables were chosen, toward the
maximum precise model to perceive fraudulent financial reporting. The multiple DM (data mining) approach achieved an accuracy of 90.83% for
fraud detection. The limitation was lower classification accuracy.
Wang et al. [18] developed a graph attentive semi-supervised (SemiGNN) network for detecting financial frauds. The detection procedure can
be processed by expanding the labeled data via social interactions in order to obtain the unlabeled data. The presented network has used both
unlabeled as well as multi-view labeled data for detecting financial frauds. However, the correlation among the diverse views and neighbors can
be done using the mechanism of hierarchical attention. The experimentation was conducted on the ALIPAY dataset. The prediction performance
was evaluated using SemiGNN on metrics KS (0.464) and AUC (0.807). The drawback was difficulty in handling the complex as well as changing

**3.1** **Data preprocessing**
In data mining, data preprocessing is the basic step which takes the raw data as input and converts it into a machine-understandable format. The
real-world and raw data can be messy and usually in the form of images, text, and videos. Moreover, the data is incomplete and includes errors as
well as inconsistencies. Therefore, data preprocessing aims to convert the unstructured data into a structured form. In this article, the data pre
processing is used to find the qualitative features from a financial statement. In data preprocessing stage, the data cleaning procedure is employed
which eliminates the noisy data. Hence, it also includes the procedures like data transformation, and reduction. Throughout the data preprocessing,
the financial statement of the documents would transform into lower cases so that could be able to avoid the attachment of same words from finan
cial statements. Thus, it also used to remove all punctuation from the statement so it can be able to classify the documents clearly. After completing
the data preprocessing method then, it undergoes with sampling process, which computes the dataset that can evaluate the verification code at
various ratio format.

**3.3** **Feature extraction**
In this work, the textual features of financial statements are combined with the data mining approaches for providing best classification of fraud in
financial statements. Text mining evaluates the text data for calculating the word frequencies. In this work, term frequency-inverse document fre
quency (TF-IDF) [29] and Word2vec are used to represent the text data. TF-IDF is a valuable weighting scheme in text mining. A term is frequent in the
number of times in a text which is denoted as the word frequency. To compute the reverse likelihood of finding a word, the IDF approach is employed
in a text. Word2vec is utilized to represent the words in the corpus as a vector by understanding the contextual information. The configuration of
Word2vec contains two methods: skip-gram and continuous bag of words (CBOW). The skip-gram aimed for predicting the contiguous words by
giving reference word as input. Instead, the contiguous words are used in CBOW for predicting the current word.
Along with these text features, some data items are also extracted from the financial statements of companies to perceive the financial fraud

mon tag information. In this work, a repeating patterns analysis is used to extract common tags or name of account from the dataset. The financial
statement of balance sheet, income statement, and statement of cash flows in the dataset contains common tags. In addition to this tag informa

**3.4** **Feature selection**
The feature selection process aims to enhance the performance of classification by minimizing the computational overhead. Here, the selection
of relevant features is performed using FRD algorithm. The presented FRD approach removes the redundant and irrelevant features. FRD based
feature selection minimizes the number of total features and the run time duration thereby enhancing the overall accuracy. The feature selection
issue related to the fraud statement detection considers multiple objective optimization problems.
In this work, the feature selection process is motivated based on meta-heuristic red deer (RD) algorithm which minimizes the cost of com
putation. Consequently, the aim of the FRD algorithm [30] is used to find the best optimal solution from the set of total features. The basic concept
of this RD optimization algorithm is inspired by the behavioral traits of red deer, and classified into various stages like roaring, mating, and
fighting. The best population is determined and named as male RD and other are called as hinds. Subsequently, harems are formed after roar
ing and fighting the female RD which prefers high to low rate of roaring. The RD algorithm comprises two phases they are intensification and
diversification.

and Somersault foraging.

**4** **SIMULATION RESULTS**
The proposed unsupervised learning approach of financial statement fraud detection is implemented in the PYTHON environment using financial
statement datasets. Also, the proposed method is compared with random forest [21] algorithm, SVM algorithm, and SVDD. [22] The evaluation metrics
used to estimate the performance of the proposed approach are accuracy, precision, recall rate, and F-measure. The detail description about the
dataset, performance metrics, and comparison parts are provided in the following subsection.
**4.1** **Dataset description**
The proposed work is validated by collecting financial statements from the FS datasets and it is available in Kaggle. These data are chosen from
the source extensible business reporting language (XBRL) tagged financial statements and filers submitted this information to commission. This
dataset contains fraudulent filings and some non-fraudulent filings of 5733 companies reported by the Securities and Exchange Commission’s (SEC)
in the year of 2015–2017. This dataset contains information regarding submissions, numbers, taxonomy tags, and presentation. The submissions
file summarizes the whole data regarding the electronic data gathering, analysis, and retrieval system (EDGAR) submission. The entire standard
taxonomytagsandcustomtaxonomytagsdescribedinthesubmissionsarecontainedintheTAGfile.Thistagfileresemblesthecommissionfinancial
statement and the necessities of schedule disclosures. All the numeric information is available in numbers file. In general, the primary financial
statements include balance sheet, income statement, cash flows, changes in equity, and comprehensive Income. The presentation file gives data
regarding the way of presentation of tags and numbers in the primary financial statements. This information is provided as rows and columns in TXT
format file. The number of fraudulent filings were 739, compared with 4994 associated with non-fraudulent filings.

The following metrics are used to validate the performance of the proposed financial fraud statement detection approach. The percent of correct
classification of samples are termed as accuracy. The TP rate (TPR) is otherwise named as sensitivity or recall. It is defined as the ratio of correct

rate (FPR) is defined as the incorrect classification of fraudulent companies. The percentage of correct classification of non-fraudulent companies
are termed as TN rate (TNR) or specificity. The percentage of incorrect classification of non-fraudulent companies is known as FN rate (FNR). The
harmonic mean of precision and TP rate is represented as F-measure. AUC represents the probability of classification model for ranking the random
selection of positive sample higher than the random selection of negative sample. The formulas for all these metrics are expressed as follows:

**5** **CONCLUSION**
In this work, an effective FS fraud detection is performed using unsupervised learning based CNN-MRFO algorithm. In the preprocessing stage,
the data cleaning process is done to clean the presence of noise. Also, data transformation, and reduction were comprised in this progression. The
SMOTE sampling process measures Kaggle dataset and it is verified through random oversampling method. The selection of financial attributes
is processed using FRD algorithm and the ADBC clustering process takes place for the grouping the entire data. After the clustering process, the
classification of data is executed using hybrid CNN-MRFO to predict the financial fraud statements. The proposed method has achieved highest
range of accuracy (98.85%), precision (98.62%), recall value (98.43%), specificity (98.58%), and F-measure (99.32%) when compared with existing
RFA, SVDD, and SVM techniques. In addition, the baseline DL classifiers such as LSTM and RNN gained lesser detection results while the proposed
CNN-MRFO approach obtained greater results on accuracy as well as with other metrics. The limitation of the proposed model is that a single
datasetisusedforexecution.Also,inthedataset,someannualreportsofthelistedcompanieshaveincompleteinformationwhichmayfurtheraffect
the prediction outcomes. Furthermore, the applicability of the detection models needs to be enhanced because the public data source may involve
Chinese, US-listed companies, eliminating those in other markets. In future, we will extend this work by executing with different datasets and try to
extract information from announcements of listed companies which can be very helpful for easy interpretation of prediction process because of rich

answers.answer: The Kaggle dataset contains 5733 companies from SEC filings in years 2015-2017
answers.rationale: This dataset contains fraudulent filings and some non-fraudulent filings of 5733 companies reported by the Securities and Exchange Commission's (SEC) in the year of 2015–2017.

answers.answer: The dataset includes 739 fraudulent filings and 4994 non-fraudulent filings
answers.rationale: The number of fraudulent filings were 739, compared with 4994 associated with non-fraudulent filings.

answers.answer: SMOTE sampling ratios are divided into 50%, 60%, and 70% normal ratio of transaction process
answers.rationale: Thus, the sample ratios are divided into 50%, 60%, and 70% normal ratio of the transaction process. SMOTE sampling for class distribution balancing

answers.answer: Six financial ratios are selected from the dataset including current ratio and quick ratio
answers.rationale: In this work, a total of six financial ratios are selected from the dataset. They are defined as follows: Current assets Current ratio = (1) Current liabilities, Quick ratio = (Cash + Marketable securities + Receivables) (2) Current liabilties

answers.answer: TF-IDF and Word2vec are used to represent the text data from financial statements
answers.rationale: In this work, term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF) and Word2vec are used to represent the text data. In this process, the text features including TF-IDF, word2vec, and financial variable data including common tag information, financial ratios are given as input to the RD optimization algorithm. In the first way of experiment, the financial statement with all the text features (TF-IDF, Word2Vec) are given as input to proposed CNN-MRFO classifier to detect fraud statement.

answers.answer: The FRD algorithm uses MAD and t-statistic as two fitness functions for feature selection
answers.rationale: The selection of features is optimized through FRD algorithm. After initializing the solutions, the candidate solutions should be measured using fitness function. The proposed feature selection problems considered two fitness functions: mean absolute difference (MAD) and t–statistic.

answers.answer: The CNN hyperparameters used are learning rate of 0.01, epochs of 32, and batch size of 20
answers.rationale: The hyperparameters used for CNN are learning rate (0.01), epochs (32), and batch size (20).

answers.answer: A Lévy flight mechanism is introduced to modify the update equation of cyclone foraging in MRFO
answers.rationale: In this article, a Lévy flight (LF) mechanism is introduced to modify the update equation of cyclone foraging. In this work, a LF approach is introduced to improve the performance of cyclone foraging behavior of MRFO.

answers.answer: The model processes XBRL tagged financial statements submitted to the SEC
answers.rationale: The proposed work is validated by collecting financial statements from the FS datasets and it is available in Kaggle. These data are chosen from the source extensible business reporting language (XBRL) tagged financial statements and filers submitted this information to commission. The submissions file summarizes the whole data regarding the electronic data gathering, analysis, and retrieval system (EDGAR) submission. The entire standard taxonomy tags and custom taxonomy tags described in the submissions are contained in the TAG file. This tag file resembles the commission financial statement and the necessities of schedule disclosures. All the numeric information is available in numbers file. In general, the primary financial statements include balance sheet, income statement, cash flows, changes in equity, and comprehensive Income. The presentation file gives data regarding the way of presentation of tags and numbers in the primary financial statements.

answers.answer: The CNN-MRFO algorithm is an unsupervised learning based algorithm.
answers.rationale: In this work, an effective FS fraud detection is performed using unsupervised learning based CNN-MRFO algorithm.

answers.answer: A limitation of the proposed model is that a single dataset is used for execution.
answers.rationale: The limitation of the proposed model is that a single dataset is used for execution.

answers.answer: ADBC algorithm increases Eps value to 0.4 if clustering fails and can process 95% of data
answers.rationale: If the algorithm fails to detect the clustering process, then it increases the value of Eps = 0.4. In this way 95% data has been exhausted by using this algorithm.

answers.answer: The MRFO algorithm divides into three foraging types: chain, cyclone and somersault foraging
answers.rationale: The formulation of MRFO has been divided into three types they are chain foraging, cyclone-foraging and Somersault foraging.
